item.title: Deadly floods sweep Albania and Montenegro as rivers burst banks
item.description: Homes surrounded by water, flooded roads and farmland submerged beneath swollen rivers. Albania and Montenegro were still battling severe flooding on Thursday, 8 January, after days of torrential rain and heavy snow.

item.title: Hundreds of farmers rally in Paris against EU-Mercosur pact and import fears
item.description: Hundreds of French farmers drive tractors into Paris to protest the EU‑Mercosur deal, warning of unfair competition and demanding stronger protections.

item.title: US aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego after record deployment
item.description: After more than 10 months at sea, the Lincoln made a stop in Thailand last month on its way back from the Middle East.

item.title: Fire rages at Yandex data centre after Ukraine drone attack
item.description: A Yandex data centre in Russia’s Ryazan region caught fire and was taken offline after what the company said was a Ukrainian drone attack.

item.title: Ex-prince Andrew warrants ruled 'unlawful' as police investigation continues
item.description: According to British media reports, it is the first time a member of the royal family has challenged the legality of criminal proceedings since the trial of Charles I in 1649.

item.title: Tsunoda Claims World Gold as Murao Retains His Title in Baku
item.description: Ai Tsunoda Roustant claimed her first senior world title at -70kg, defeating Michaela Polleres in golden score. At -90kg, Sanshiro Murao delivered a spectacular ippon against Goki Tajima in an all-Japanese final, defending his title to become a two-time world champion.

item.title: Taxes account for over 53% of labour costs in Spain, study finds
item.description: In 2025, Spain's Finance Ministry argued that its tax cuts for middle-income earners had delivered €38 billion in savings

item.title: Pro-Russian hacker group NoName targets Italian Foreign Ministry website
item.description: Checks are under way on the websites of Italian embassies and consulates abroad following a suspected similar cyberattack by pro-Russian hackers

item.title: EU debates harsh working conditions for fishers: 'I had no other choice'
item.description: Endless weeks, shifts of up to 24 hours and even no drinking water: these were some of the hardships aired last week at a debate held by the EU Fisheries Committee with sector representatives.

item.title: Mélenchon declares ‘Bastille retaken’ after major student rally in Paris
item.description: The mass student-led movement emerged over a range of issues including long school days, overcrowded schools, teacher absences.

item.title: Drought: groundwater levels in France remain very low
item.description: France's groundwater levels remain deeply worrying at the start of October: two-thirds of monitoring sites are below normal and 81% are still falling. The autumn recharge, vital to rebuild reserves, has yet to get under way.

item.title: Astronaut Sophie Adenot returns to Earth after record space mission
item.description: Sophie Adenot left the International Space Station on Wednesday after an eight-month stay, the longest by a European astronaut, and splashed down on Thursday at around 5.30 pm with three fellow crew members.

item.title: Italy probes gaming giant Activision Blizzard over in-game spending by children
item.description: Italy’s antitrust authority is investigating whether monetisation practices in Call of Duty Mobile and Diablo Immortal amount to a “widespread infringement” of EU consumer protection rules, particularly in relation to children.

item.title: US charges former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro with torture
item.description: The revised indictment includes several mentions of the involvement of Venezuela’s feared DGCIM military intelligence agency

item.title: Tiny turtles take their first steps towards the sea
item.description: On Mataking Island in Malaysia, conservationists raise and release green turtle hatchlings, part of long-running efforts that helped the species recover.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 8th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 8th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: The best 50 bars in the world have been revealed for 2026 – and 18 are in Europe
item.description: Europe dominates this year’s 50 Best ranking, with 18 bars making the top 50 and Paris overtaking London as the continent’s best-represented city. Hong Kong’s Bar Leone retains the global crown, while Milan’s Moebius Milano and Athens’ Line also break into the top five.

item.title: Heavy autumn snow paralyses roads in Russia’s Far East
item.description: Heavy autumn snowfall has paralysed roads in Russia’s Magadan region, leaving trucks struggling through snow and disrupting intercity bus services.

item.title: Marco Rubio calls Portugal 'ideal gateway' to Europe for US during Lisbon visit
item.description: As one of the smallest members of NATO and the European Union, Portugal is keen to cultivate its relations with bigger countries

item.title: EU diplomatic arm under fire for bowing to US pressure over disinformation conference
item.description: The EU diplomatic service pulled its backing from a disinformation conference after US pressure, angering MEPs and NGOs who say it undermines the bloc's own defence of civil society.

item.title: EU faces gas shortfall of up to 15% if severe winter hits, report warns
item.description: The EU is entering the winter season on thin ice, facing a double-edged geopolitical squeeze that threatens to expose the fragility of its post-Russian energy architecture.

item.title: French students clash with police as school protests continue
item.description: Students clash with police outside French schools as blockades, tear gas and fires mark a new nationwide mobilisation ahead of the 2027 election.

item.title: Experts in Baku urge action as missing persons surge worldwide and in Ukraine
item.description: Around 280,000 people are registered as missing in Ukraine alone, with 10,000 new cases added each month, part of a 70% global rise since 2019. Forensic experts meeting in Baku said the obstacle was not forensic capacity but governmental reluctance.

item.title: The disease that once ravaged Europe still exists: could plague return to Spain?
item.description: The death of a scientist in Russia has reignited fears of plague. Spain has seen no local cases for decades, yet the disease persists elsewhere. How real is the risk in Europe?

item.title: Italy approves Meloni's electoral reform in confidence vote ahead of 2027 election
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies has passed electoral law reform by 227 votes to 164, despite possible Constitutional Court objections. Italy now formally enters the election campaign, with an early vote increasingly likely.

item.title: Turkmenistan marks 35 years of independence with an eye on the future
item.description: Turkmenistan celebrated 35 years of independence with a vast parade through Ashgabat, as the country set out its ambitions for the decades ahead.

item.title: Michael Jackson memorabilia including iconic Thriller jacket to go under the hammer
item.description: Michael Jackson’s iconic fashion is going under the hammer, with more than 100 pieces from his career set to be auctioned in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Royal Navy sailor faces court over alleged spying for Russia
item.description: Royal Navy sailor appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday after being held in custody since his arrest on Tuesday at his home near London

item.title: Iran strikes tankers outside Hormuz in signs of expanding campaign
item.description: Two commercial vessels were hit within 24 hours — one off Qatar, the first attack in that area in six months, and one off Fujairah in the Gulf of Oman — as IRGC-affiliated outlets suggested Tehran had extended operations beyond the crucial strait.

item.title: EU presses Russia for more details on suspected plague case
item.description: Pressure mounts on Moscow to explain the suspected plague case in Siberia, which has put health authorities on edge. Brussels is calling on Moscow to come clean with precise details "as soon as possible".

item.title: Germany lifts GDP forecast as economy withstands Iran war
item.description: The government lifted its full-year growth projection to 1.3%, up from its April forecast of just 0.5%, as the German economy proved more resilient than expected.

item.title: OE2027: youth housing guarantee stays, defence hits 2.15% of GDP, €1m for AI
item.description: The government on Thursday submitted to parliament the 2027 state budget, projecting 2% growth and a surplus of 0.1–0.2% of GDP. Approval is assured, as the PS will abstain in the key vote.

item.title: From oil to renewables: this country's energy giant looks beyond its borders
item.description: Azerbaijan is expanding its international energy portfolio through renewable projects, strategic partnerships and new infrastructure, as it seeks to strengthen energy security and connect regional markets with Europe.

item.title: Scientists in Austria and China create the world’s first nuclear clocks. Here’s why it matters
item.description: The new nuclear clocks measure time by using lasers to make subatomic particles.

item.title: Exclusive: G7’s 100-million-barrel pledge tied to unfinished March emergency oil release
item.description: The October G7 announcement aims to accelerate and complete the IEA’s March emergency oil-stock release, rather than add a new 100-million-barrel pledge to the original 400 million, according to a document seen by Euronews.

item.title: Ethiopian drones hit Eritrean forces accused of backing rebels in Tigray
item.description: Drone strikes hit Eritrean vehicles around the northern city of Adigrat overnight, with witnesses reporting destroyed lorries and retreating troops, days after Ethiopia expelled Eritrean diplomats and Eritrea severed ties.

item.title: Kazakhstan seeks to build an AI-powered economy and manufacturing sector
item.description: Kazakhstan wants artificial intelligence to become more than a digital tool: the country is seeking to make it a new engine of economic growth, from universities and factories to energy and infrastructure.

item.title: Pink hair and powerful plaids: Tate Britain celebrates the chaotic creativity of 90s culture
item.description: Tate Britain's nostalgic new showcase highlights a lost era of optimism, rebellion and culture-defining creativity.

item.title: Manny Pacquiao hosts Polish president Karol Nawrocki for Manila boxing workout
item.description: Polish President Karol Nawrocki trains in Manila with boxing legend Manny Pacquiao, who now leads the Philippines’ National Anti-Poverty Commission.

item.title: Fresh day of student protests across France as rally planned in Paris
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu addressed the nation on Wednesday evening in an effort to ease the crisis, promising the government would share a plan to respond to the situation by the end of October.

item.title: Gulf economies to shrink despite higher oil prices as Iran war takes toll, World Bank says
item.description: The Iran war has hit two mainstays of Gulf business: energy exports and aviation. The disruption extends to Europe, where buyers have had to replace missing gas supplies.

item.title: Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
item.description: Anne Carson was among the bookies' favourites to win this year, as her body of work eschews easy categorisation.The Nobel Prize committee singled out her “bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature.”

item.title: South Korea recalls ambassador to Ukraine in North Korean prisoner of war row
item.description: Seoul said Kyiv's public disclosure of the repatriation of two North Korean prisoners endangered their families in North Korea, where relatives of those who fall into enemy hands face punishment. Ukraine has rejected South Korea's accusations.

item.title: Two-thirds of young Europeans suffered childhood trauma, with lasting life impact, WHO finds
item.description: Two-thirds of European children experienced trauma that ‘follows them into the classroom, job market and their relationships’.

item.title: Tallinn Airport lets driverless shuttles run close to airplanes, opening the way to wider airport automation
item.description: Euronews Next exclusive: A driverless shuttle now carries aircraft workers and spare parts at Tallinn Airport, with no safety agents on board.

item.title: EU debt could hit €1 trillion by 2027 as spending errors rise, auditors warn
item.description: EU auditors said 3.8% of the bloc's spending last year breached funding rules, warning that borrowing could hit €1 trillion by 2027 and that the next long-term budget risks repeating the flaws of the COVID-era recovery fund, as the Commission defended its controls.

item.title: Portuguese hospital lets pets visit owners on wards: a new model?
item.description: In northern and central Europe, pets stay outside hospitals. São João's flexible model unites clinical benefits and safety, with no infections yet. "There is too much fear," says the doctor who helped draft the project's rules.

item.title: Ryanair CEO sees no European jet fuel shortages into summer 2027
item.description: Ryanair CEO Michael O’Leary expects Europe to have enough jet fuel through next summer, but warns that high prices will persist for another 12 to 18 months.

item.title: “I settled eight wars”: Trump says he deserves Nobel Peace Prize
item.description: Donald Trump says he deserves the Nobel Peace Prize, citing his efforts to resolve international conflicts.

item.title: UK airport e-gates to become passport-free and contactless by early 2027
item.description: UK airports have begun rolling out contactless e-gates. The technology allows eligible travellers to pass through without having to show their passports.
